cases.title: East Coast Rail Link: homes cleared and flooded at Gombak
cases.place: Kampung Sungai Chinchin and Desa Mukmin, Gombak Utara, Selangor, Malaysia
cases.point: Kampung Sungai Chinchin, Gombak, in the Selayang municipal area (OpenStreetMap via Nominatim); approximate for the case as a whole, which covers villages across Gombak Utara including Desa Mukmin and Kampung Sungai Salak

lenders.name: China Eximbank
lenders.role: Preferential buyer's credit to Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd for Phase 1 of the East Coast Rail Link. AidData's records, read on 15 November 2026, say China Eximbank and Malaysia Rail Link signed a preferential buyer's credit worth RMB 61.88 billion (RM 39.1 billion) on or around 1 April 2017, and that the loan reportedly carried a 20-year maturity, a 7-year grace period and a fixed 3.25% interest rate, with a grant element of 46.99% and Malaysia's Ministry of Finance as guarantor. AidData files the Phase 1 credit under two record numbers without saying how either relates to that RM 39.1 billion: record 85858, the revised Phase 1 loan at an estimated RM 37.7 billion, commitment date 1 April 2017, status implementation; and record 73473, the cancelled portion at RM 37.4 billion, commitment date 17 August 2017, status cancelled. Record 49309 holds a later pledge for Phases 1 and 2. As of August 2018 the borrower had drawn RM 19.69 billion, a disbursement rate of 50.3%, of which RM 10.02 billion was an advance payment to the contractor and RM 9.67 billion a progress payment; the amount outstanding was about US$3.264 billion (RM 13.6 billion) on 31 December 2018. Malaysia's transport minister told a parliamentary oversight body in July 2022 that the grace period had been extended to 2027 and the interest rate was unchanged (AidData, records 85858 and 73473).

cases.conditions: The credit was to pay 85% of the cost of the 1 November 2016 commercial contract between Malaysia Rail Link and China Communications Construction Company, worth RMB 72.8 billion (RM 46 billion), so the money was spent with the lender's own state contractor. 60% was to be made available in renminbi and 40% in ringgit. The Government of Malaysia gave a sovereign guarantee. When Malaysia cancelled the project in August 2018, China Eximbank told the new government it could either renegotiate the contracts or pay termination costs of about RM 21.78 billion; the government renegotiated, and a supplemental agreement on 12 April 2019 cut the cost from RM 65.5 billion to RM 44 billion and set up a 50:50 joint venture with the contractor to run the line. China Eximbank eventually agreed to finance 75% of the project cost, the remaining 25% to be raised through local sukuk (AidData, records 85858 and 73473).

companies.name: China Communications Construction Co. (CCCC)
companies.role: Engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contractor for the railway, working in Malaysia as China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd, which is one of three defendants in a 2026 High Court claim over damage to a house at Gombak (AidData; New Straits Times)
companies.desc: Chinese state-owned transport infrastructure group, incorporated on 8 October 2006 and founded by China Communications Construction Group (CCCG). It designs and builds ports, roads, bridges, railways and tunnels and also does dredging, heavy machinery manufacturing and international contracting, with more than 60 subsidiaries as of 2019.

companies.name: Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL)
companies.role: Borrower and owner of the railway; offered the ex-gratia money at Desa Mukmin with the state government, and agreed to cover rent for 21 households at Sungai Chinchin and repairs to homes and roads there (AidData; Sinar Harian; Selangor Journal)
companies.desc: A state company set up on 26 September 2016 as a wholly owned subsidiary and special purpose vehicle of Minister of Finance Incorporated, the corporate arm of Malaysia's Ministry of Finance. It was created to design, finance, build and maintain the East Coast Rail Link, and is the line's 100% owner during construction (AidData).

cases.community: A census by Selangor's Department of the Director General of Lands and Mines on 21 November 2023 confirmed 135 structures in the railway's path at Desa Mukmin in Gombak, and that those 135 structures held 157 heads of household. The department and the Gombak District and Land Office issued an order to clear the site on Wednesday 13 December 2023, with a deadline of 15 January 2024. The payments offered to the owners and tenants told to vacate were RM 3,000 in moving costs, RM 1,500 a month in rent for 24 months and compensation for the structure, with a choice of 49 Rumah Selangorku units at Bandar Tasik Puteri priced at RM 79,000 or places in the state's SmartSewa rental programme at two sites, 40 units at Blok Temenggung and 240 at Sri Damai. Two residents said they accepted the order, one of them that the RM 3,000 eased the move (Sinar Harian). Residents said they were told in late November that they had 20 days to leave, and that the government planned to demolish their homes and about 100 others in the village; officers of the lands and mines department and a spokesperson for China Communications Construction (ECRL) declined to answer questions about the short notice, and the chief minister's office did not reply (BenarNews, 6 December 2023). At Kampung Sungai Salak, named residents said flash floods started after trees and the hillside behind the village were cleared, and one said flood water came through her kitchen door; the project team said its site clearing there had begun on 7 June 2023. At Kampung Sungai Chinchin, villagers said piling work less than 100 metres from the houses had cracked walls and broken floor tiles in several homes and in the Tabika Kemas Batu 7 kindergarten, whose teacher said the cracks appeared after the piling started; the project team said the piling began on 21 September (Malaysiakini, 11 October 2023). On 21 October 2024 Selangor Journal reported that a retention pond would be built at Sungai Chinchin after flash floods “resulting from the ongoing construction”, that the chief minister had instructed the authorities to help temporarily relocate 21 houses in low-lying areas to rented homes at Malaysia Rail Link's cost, and that Malaysia Rail Link had agreed to bear the cost of repairing damage to homes and roads caused by material explosions. The chief minister was quoted saying the works had affected residents of Sungai Chinchin and Gombak Utara, and listing more frequent flash floods, noise, air and dust pollution and burst pipes (Selangor Journal; The Star). Free Malaysia Today reported on 24 February 2024 that the chief minister was responding to a news report that some 2,500 residents of 13 villages in Gombak intended to file an injunction after 151 homes were demolished for the project; the article names no source for that figure and gives no date for the demolitions (Free Malaysia Today).
cases.displaced_note: Sinar Harian gives 135 structures in the alignment at Desa Mukmin, holding 157 heads of household, under an order to vacate by 15 January 2024; The Star, reporting the same ex-gratia payments, says the 157 heads of household “will have to relocate”. Free Malaysia Today, citing an unnamed news report, says 151 homes were demolished, and gives no date for the demolitions. The first counts structures and household heads ordered to move, the second counts houses; neither is a count of people moved.
cases.ecosystem: Residents at Kampung Sungai Salak said flash floods began after trees and the hillside behind the village were cleared for the works, and that floods now follow within an hour of rain (Malaysiakini). A private geologist engaged by one Gombak family in August 2024 reported high water saturation in the hillslope beside their house, and a later soil study commissioned by the family concluded the chance of the slope collapsing was very high (New Straits Times).
cases.outcome: The Selangor government, with Malaysia Rail Link, handed the ex-gratia payments to the Desa Mukmin recipients at a ceremony at Dewan Beringin Sri Gombak on the Thursday after the clearance order of Wednesday 13 December 2023 (Sinar Harian, 14 December 2023; The Star, 18 December 2023). A retention pond was ordered for Sungai Chinchin in October 2024, and Malaysia Rail Link committed to suspending work there on Sundays and on days such as examination periods (Selangor Journal). A couple at Gombak filed a RM 1.33 million claim in the High Court on 24 April 2026 against China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd, Malaysia Rail Link and the Selayang Municipal Council, saying hillslope work since early 2024 made their house shake. They said a dilapidation survey was done only in February 2024 after repeated complaints, that the contractor and Malaysia Rail Link told them the environmental assessment and site investigation reports were in the public domain and they had to find them themselves, that the municipal council ordered a full study in early 2025 while Malaysia Rail Link said in March 2025 that the existing studies were enough, that a letter of demand in October 2025 was refused, and that three other houses were affected. The paper said it had asked all three defendants for comment (New Straits Times, 12 July 2026). Passenger services are scheduled for 2027.

cases.confidence_note: The eviction and demolition counts come from Malaysian press reports, and the figure of 151 homes is Free Malaysia Today's account of an unnamed news report rather than a government count. The project team, Malaysia Rail Link and China Communications Construction (ECRL), told Malaysiakini that Kampung Sungai Salak had flooded for close to a decade before its works began, citing a 2014 report, that its site clearing there began on 7 June 2023, that it had received no official complaint of cracked walls, and that it chose bored piling to keep vibration and noise down. A year later Selangor Journal, the Selangor government's news site, reported the flash floods as resulting from the construction and the company as agreeing to pay for damage caused by material explosions; that causal wording is the paper's own and not a quotation from the chief minister, who was quoted saying the works had affected residents. The claims in the 2026 High Court case have not been tested. The chief minister also said in February 2024 that outsiders were inciting residents against the project (Free Malaysia Today). AidData has restated the two loan records: an earlier version of their text split the RM 39.1 billion Phase 1 loan into RM 19.69 billion disbursed (record 85858) and RM 19.41 billion cancelled (record 73473), while the version read on 15 November 2026 gives RM 37.7 billion and RM 37.4 billion and does not explain the change.
cases.whole: The line was not yet carrying passengers: in July 2026 passenger services were still scheduled for 2027 (New Straits Times). Malaysia's transport minister told Parliament in September that the project was nearly 54% built and well placed to finish by 2027 (BenarNews, 6 December 2023), and AidData's record puts it at 62.4% complete as of July 2024. Reported lengths differ: 655 km (BenarNews), 665 km (Malaysiakini and New Straits Times), while AidData's record gives 688 km for the railway and 600.3 km for Phase 1. AidData's records put the drawn part of the credit at RM 19.69 billion by August 2018, the cost cut to RM 44 billion under the April 2019 supplemental agreement, and then a rescoped total of RM 50.27 billion announced in April 2021, of which China Eximbank is financing 75%, or RM 37.7 billion. No measure of what the line delivers to Gombak was found.

fields_add.conditions: AidData's record, read on 15 November 2026, states that the loan was collateralised against the future sales receipts of the project company SOGES S.A. and against a minimum cash balance in a lender-controlled escrow account, beginning at US$20 million and rising to US$90 million; the borrower was expected to meet the US$20 million minimum by March 2021. Guinea also issued a sovereign guarantee for the loan and guaranteed the payment obligations of the state utility EDG to SOGES under a power purchase agreement, whose proceeds from 20 years of electricity sales were to repay the loan. Guinea covered the 15% of the project cost it had to fund itself by selling its 51% stake in SOGEKA, the company running the Kaleta dam, to China Three Gorges for US$200 million on 2 November 2016 (AidData, record 187).

fields_add.conditions: AidData's record, read on 15 November 2026, gives the US$700 million facility signed on 15 December 2015 a five-year grace period and a 6.5% fixed interest rate, and gives its maturity two ways: 17 years in the record's loan-terms panel and 17.5 years in its narrative. The same record says an amendment of 6 November 2019 reset the rate to six-month LIBOR plus 300 basis points when LIBOR was above 1.5% a year and plus 350 basis points when it was below, and a second amendment of 15 December 2022 to plus 280 and plus 330; as of 31 December 2022 the rate was six-month LIBOR plus 280 basis points. The facility was secured on all the perpetual leasehold rights in the land and all the plant's machinery and equipment, and on the stakes that Royal Group Power and EVN International hold in Hydro Power Lower Sesan 2, and was guaranteed by Huaneng Lancang River Hydropower, the ultimate parent of the 51% shareholder (AidData, record 62217).

The credit, signed on 11 September 2013, is numbered China Eximbank PBC No. (2013) 38, total no. (282), and ran 20 years with an 11-year grace period at 2% interest, with no default interest, a 0.25% commitment fee and a 0.18% management fee. Its proceeds were to finance a commercial contract of the same value, US$386 million, numbered D-166-21/322, between the joint-stock company Electric Power Plants of Kyrgyzstan and TBEA. The Kyrgyz government's aid management platform records a first disbursement of US$115.8 million on 31 December 2014, 30% of the loan. Kyrgyz finance ministry data given to AidData in July 2022 show the loan fully disbursed, with US$389,924,333.33 outstanding on 31 December 2021, more than the principal because deferred principal and interest were added to the body of the debt. China Eximbank suspended principal and interest due between 1 July and 31 December 2021 under a debt suspension agreement, a period the record's staff note instead gives as August to December 2021 (AidData, record 39620, read on 15 November 2026).

AidData's record, read on 15 November 2026, adds that, according to China Development Bank, US$367 million was disbursed under the US$473 million loan by the end of 2014, and puts the whole plant's cost at US$638 million, financed with a mix of debt and equity (AidData, record 49810).

extend.whole_replace: Djawanews reported in 2020, without naming a source, that the plant supplied about 43% of Bali's electricity; it describes three units of 142 MW but gives the total as 380 MW. Mongabay gives 426 MW and quotes a Huadian director saying the plant can meet two-fifths of Bali's demand. AidData's record says that as of 17 May 2017 the plant had generated 5.2 billion kilowatt hours, accounting for 40% of Bali's total power supply and allowing Bali to stop relying on power generation and supply from Java; the record names no source for that sentence, and the sources it lists for the project include Chinese state-enterprise and Huadian publications. In 2018 the energy ministry's site reported 1,280 MW of supply for Bali against an average daily peak of 863 MW, in a report on the state utility's Bali manager. No independent check of the plant's output was found.
